requirements.title: List-directed null values are r*, empty fields, or leading empty first fields
requirements.definition: A null value is specified by r*, by no characters between consecutive value separators, or by no characters before the first value separator in the first record read for the input statement.

pending.repeat-null-form: Initialize integer x=9; internal READ record '1*' into x; expected x remains 9.
pending.empty-between-separators: Initialize integer array [1,2,3]; internal READ record '10,,30'; expected values [10,2,30].
pending.leading-empty-first-record: Initialize integers x=7,y=8; internal READ record ',9' into x,y; expected x remains 7 and y becomes 9.

requirements.title: List-directed null values preserve definition status and cannot be complex parts
requirements.definition: A null value has no effect on the next effective item definition status; it shall not be used for either complex part, but one null may represent an entire complex constant.

pending.null-preserves-value: Initialize integer x=7; internal READ record ',' into x followed by another item; expected x remains 7.
pending.single-null-entire-complex: Initialize complex z=(1.0,2.0); internal READ record ',' into z followed by another item; expected z remains approximately (1.0,2.0).
pending.null-not-complex-part: Deferred input-error plan: '(,2.0)' differs from '(1.0,2.0)' only by a null real part; observe IOSTAT if Clause 12 makes it portable, not a diagnostic.

requirements.title: Slash terminates list-directed input and null-supplies remaining effective items
requirements.definition: A slash value separator terminates the input statement after the previous value, ignores the rest of the record, and supplies null values for additional effective items and input-list do-variables as needed.

pending.slash-terminates: Initialize x=-1,y=-2; internal READ record '1 / 99' into x,y; expected x=1 and y remains -2.
pending.slash-ignores-rest: Same record '1 / not_an_integer' into x,y; expected no attempt to parse trailing text after slash when portable IOSTAT context is supplied.
pending.slash-null-supplies-remaining: Initialize integer array [5,6,7]; internal READ record '1 /' into all elements; expected [1,6,7].

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review, two rounds: doc/source_audits/batch_139.json. This COMPLETES the list-directed and namelist half of Clause 13. The reviewer re-derived unit hashes, re-partitioned the four sections sharing PDF p312 unit by unit, verified the zero-numbered-R/C claim across all 77 units, re-read both note result tables row-by-row (13.10.3.2 NOTE 3 and 13.11.3.6 NOTE), and confirmed 13.10.4 contains no table despite being the flagged candidate. THE CRUX of this scope is the REQUIRED versus PROCESSOR-DEPENDENT split, and the reviewer audited it in BOTH directions, producing two blocking findings that are the same error in mirror image. C139SR-001: the F/E choice for real list-directed output was marked WHOLLY processor-dependent, but 13.10.4 p5 fixes one case - a real ZERO must use F form - so the claim was TOO BROAD, which is itself a defect; the unit is now split, with a required facet asserting ONLY the form (no E-form exponent marker) and explicitly not the width, digits, sign or decimal spelling, and 13.11.4.2 propagating it through namelist editing. C139SR-002 ran the other way: a plan asserted the exact substring I= while the same packet marked spacing around equals processor-dependent, and a conforming processor may emit I with a space; the plan now asserts the uppercase object-name token only. The genuine obligations survive and were hand-verified including their leading blanks: ' T' and ' F' from 13.10.4 p3 with p13, ' AB' for delimiter mode NONE from p8, and the namelist prefix ' &G' from 13.11.4.3 p3 and p5. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1977, no fixture bound, no compiler invoked.
